## 0. Data prep
```{r}
tt_var <- read_xlsx("/Users/langgao/Downloads/Freelancer projects/Sonder/North_Nigeria_2024DHS8_1.0/output/pathways workbook - North_Nigeria_2024DHS8_1.0.xlsx",sheet = 'vulnerabilities')
tt.var.rural <- tt_var$vulnerability_variable[tt_var$typing_tool_include ==1 & tt_var$typing_tool_strata%in%c("both", "rural")]
tt.var.urban <- tt_var$vulnerability_variable[tt_var$typing_tool_include ==1 & tt_var$typing_tool_strata%in%c("both", "urban")]

tt.var.rural
tt.var.urban
```

### 0.1. Rural subset (5-class)
```{r}
tt_input_names.r <- names(rural)[(names(rural) %in% c("segment_rank", tt.var.rural))]
rural_seg <- subset(rural, select=c(tt_input_names.r))
# tt_input_names.r
rural_seg <- rural_seg %>% 
  dplyr::select(-"polygamy")
```

### 0.2. Urban sebset (4-class)
```{r}
tt_input_names.u <- names(urban)[(names(urban) %in% c("segment_rank", tt.var.urban))]
urban_seg <- subset(urban, select=c(tt_input_names.u))
dim(urban_seg)
```

set as factor
```{r}
rural_seg$segment_rank <- as.factor(rural_seg$segment_rank)
urban_seg$segment_rank <- as.factor(urban_seg$segment_rank)
```

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
```

## 1. Rural tree
```{r}
# table(rural_seg$segment_rank, rural_seg$polygamy)
```

### 1.1. Grow tree with penalty

```{r}
#  Grow a tree with loss penalty for R4.1 and R2 
cls <- levels(rural_seg$segment_rank)
K   <- length(cls)

loss <- matrix(1, nrow = K, ncol = K, dimnames = list(cls, cls))
diag(loss) <- 0
loss["R4.1-NN", ] <- 1   # stronger penalty for harder segment
loss["R4.1-NN", "R4.1-NN"] <- 0
loss["R2-NN",   ] <- 0.8
loss["R2-NN",   "R2-NN"]   <- 0

tree_rural <- rpart(segment_rank ~ .,  data=rural_seg, parms = list(loss = loss), control=rpart.control(cp=0.001, xval=5), method="class")


# See what is the cp value if following 1-SE rule 
cp_table <- as.data.frame(tree_rural$cptable)
# minimum xerror row
min_row <- which.min(cp_table$xerror)
# threshold = min xerror + its standard error
threshold <- cp_table$xerror[min_row] + cp_table$xstd[min_row]

# pick the LARGEST cp (= simplest tree) whose xerror is still within threshold
cp_1se <- cp_table$CP[max(which(cp_table$xerror <= threshold))]

cat("cp chosen by 1-SE rule:", cp_1se, "\n")
cat("cp chosen by min-xerror:", cp_table$CP[min_row], "\n")
#both suggesting 0.001 (earlier when penalizing, we use the xerror: tree_loss$cptable[which.min(tree_loss$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"], it also indicates 0.001; but then the tree is still big, so adjust it to 0.0015)
tree_rural_prune <- prune(tree_rural, cp = 0.0018)
```

### 1.2. Finan rural tree and performance
```{r, fig.height=12, fig.width=20}
prp(tree_rural_prune, type=5, varlen=0, cex=0.9, extra = 2)

pred <- predict(tree_rural_prune, rural_seg, type = "class")
confusionMatrix(pred, rural_seg$segment_rank)
```

### 1.2.3. Save
```{r}
saveRDS(tree_rural_prune, "CART/tree_rural_pruned.rds")
```


Previous model for reference/compare [not to use]
```{r,eval=FALSE}
tree_rural <- rpart(segment_rank ~ .,  data=rural_seg, control=rpart.control(cp=0.001, xval=5), method="class")

plotcp(tree_rural)
printcp(tree_rural)
#Variables actually used in tree construction (19)      
```

```{r, fig.height=15, fig.width=12, eval=FALSE}
tree_rural_prune<-prune(tree_rural, cp=tree_rural$cptable[which.min(tree_rural$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"])
tree_rural_prune<-prune(tree_rural, cp=0.0039)
```

```{r, fig.height=12, fig.width=18, eval=FALSE}
prp(tree_rural_prune, type=5, varlen=0, cex=1)

PredictCART_train_rural <- predict(tree_rural_prune, data=rural_seg, type="class")
PredictCART_train_rural <- as.factor(PredictCART_train_rural)
confusionMatrix(data=PredictCART_train_rural, rural_seg$segment_rank)
```


Previous CART with loss matrix penalizing only R4.1
```{r}
#penalize is takes involving R4.1-NN
  ##increase sensitivity of R4.1-NN (to reduce false negative)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
cls <- levels(rural_seg$segment_rank)
K <- length(cls)

loss <- matrix(1, nrow = K, ncol = K, dimnames = list(cls, cls))
diag(loss) <- 0

target <- "R4.1-NN"
# Penalize false negatives for R4.1-NN
loss[target, ] <- 1.2
loss[target, target] <- 0

tree_loss <- rpart(
  segment_rank ~ .,
  data = rural_seg,
  method = "class",
  parms = list(loss = loss),
  control = rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 5))

# Prune by xerror (or try 1-SE rule later)
cp_best <- tree_loss$cptable[which.min(tree_loss$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"]
# cp_best
tree_loss_pruned <- prune(tree_loss, cp = cp_best)

pred <- predict(tree_loss_pruned, rural_seg, type = "class")
confusionMatrix(pred, rural_seg$segment_rank)
```

```{r, fig.height=10, fig.width=22, eval=FALSE}
prp(tree_loss_pruned, type = 5, varlen = 0, cex = 0.8, extra = 2)

```


## 2. Urban tree
### 2.1. Grow tree
```{r, echo=TRUE}
tree_urban <- rpart(segment_rank ~ .,  data=urban_seg, control=rpart.control(cp=0.001, xval=5), method="class")

plotcp(tree_urban)
#Use cp = 0.0081 (using 0.0053 does not necessarily improve the matrix sign., in additional, 0.0081 provides the matrix that meet the thresthold)

printcp(tree_urban)
#Variables actually used in tree construction (13)        
```

### 2.2. Prune tree [FINAL urban tree]
```{r, fig.height=15, fig.width=12}
tree_urban_prune<-prune(tree_urban, cp=tree_urban$cptable[which.min(tree_urban$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"])
tree_urban_prune<-prune(tree_urban, cp=.0081)
#plot(tree_urban_prune, uniform=TRUE, main="Classification Tree for Urban LCA")
#text(tree_urban_prune, use.n=TRUE, all=TRUE, cex=.7)
```

```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width= 12}
prp(tree_urban_prune, type = 5, varlen = 0, cex = 0.8, extra = 2)

PredictCART_train_urban <- predict(tree_urban_prune, data=urban_seg, type="class")
PredictCART_train_urban <- as.factor(PredictCART_train_urban)
confusionMatrix(data=PredictCART_train_urban, urban_seg$segment_rank)
```

### 2.3. Save pruned tree
```{r}
saveRDS(tree_urban_prune, "CART/tree_urban_pruned.rds")
```
